stem:
Ayaan compares a camel in a dry desert with a mountain goat on rocky slopes. The camel has wide padded feet; the goat has strong hooves that grip rock.

Which statements treat these features as adaptations for survival in each region? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Wide padded feet help the camel walk on soft sand in the desert.
Strong gripping hooves help the mountain goat move on rocky slopes.
Wide padded feet help the camel only because they look unusual, not because they suit soft sand.
Any body part of the goat is an adaptation for rocky slopes, even parts that do not help it grip or move there.

teacher.key_rationale: An adaptation is a feature that helps survival in a particular region: padded feet suit soft sand; gripping hooves suit rocky slopes. Unusual looks alone do not make a feature an adaptation, and not every body part is an adaptation for that habitat.
